text:
alex: Heads up — noticed a perf regression after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak (commit abc123). nvprof/nsys traces look different. Sharing quick highlights.

morgan: oof, numbers? rough magnitude?

alex: From a 200-token run on p3.16x: tail latency P95 went from 210ms -> 320ms. Throughput down ~18% on steady load. KV cache hit ratio dropped from 87% -> 68% for that trace set.

jia: that's pretty big. did the selector choose a new kernel family for MatMul or Attention?

alex: selector started preferring kernel v2 (int8-fused) for medium sequence lengths after the change. v2 reduces flops but introduced an extra device-side memcpy in the hotpath when sequence < 128. nvprof timeline shows memcpy + kernel serialized instead of overlapping.

sam: can you paste the nsys command and the two timelines (before/after) exports? I can diff.

alex: sure — run we used:
```
nsys profile --output trace-before --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --duration=20s ./run_infer --model redwood-v1 --batch-size 8
nsys profile --output trace-after  --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --duration=20s ./run_infer --model redwood-v1 --batch-size 8
```
I exported the timeline slices to JSON and looked at kernel name patterns. Before: `matmul_fused_v1` overlapped memcpyD2D+compute. After: `matmul_fused_v2` does `memcpy_async` then `matmul`, no overlap.

morgan: any kernel time numbers? CONTRIBUTION per-kernel?

alex: yes — quick grep from the exported timeline:
```
# before
matmul_fused_v1 total: 42.3ms, overlap memcpy: ~12.1ms, effective compute: 30.2ms
# after
matmul_fused_v2 total: 52.9ms, memcpy: 15.8ms (serialized), compute: 37.1ms
```
So a ~10ms delta per call, ~18% across throughput given call frequency.

jia: why did the selector pick v2 for seq<128? I thought v2 was supposed to be faster for short seqs.

alex: selector scoring used an outdated perf table — the recent microbenchmarking on new drivers bumped v1 with kernel-launch overlap improvements. The config accidentally flipped priority for the medium-bin. Also KV cache behavior: after v2, we observed more prefix re-materializations because v2's prefetch path expects contiguous KV layout; mismatch caused extra cache misses in 1/6 of requests.

sam: can we replicate with a tight harness and bisect commits between abc100..abc140? I can automate.

perf-bot: run triggered — bisect harness queue created (id: 6172). Pulling commit range abc100..abc140.

morgan: good. also check batcher heuristics — maybe concurrent batch grouping changed with the new kernel latency profile.

alex: already ran microbenchmark for batcher: batching window fixed at 6ms; with v2 that window causes 2 extra batches per second where latency stretches and reduces peak pack size by 12%. Proposed short-term fix: revert selector priority for medium-bin -> restore v1 preference; long-term: update selector scoring to include memcpy/overlap metric and KV layout compatibility flag.

jia: i can own the selector scoring patch. Sam — if you automate bisect, add a probe that records: kernel chosen, memcpy bytes, KV cache hits, batch sizes per request. That will pinpoint the commit that introduced the regression.

sam: on it. will spin up 20 bisect jobs with nsys capture (first 5s) and aggregate. ETA ~2h.

alex: thanks. saving nvprof exports to /mnt/perf/artifacts/1851987654/ (before.json, after.json, batcher-sample.log). I'll attach summary to the bisect results.

morgan: ping @jia when you open the PR for selector scoring. if bisect pins it to one commit, we hotfix revert asap.

jia: will do. thx.

sam: bisect job started. will post results and a minimal reproducer snippet once we have the guilty commit.

alex: :thumbsup: quick note — keep an eye on driver versions. this only showed up on CUDA 12.1 nodes; older 11.x weren't affected.

morgan: good catch. tag infra for a node matrix run too.

perf-bot: bisect job 6172: started. updates in #eng-runtime.

alex: ok closing here for now — will update thread when bisect yields a single commit.
